reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Rebuilt the Dutch bachelor from adopted OER B4.2, B4.3, B4.5 and B7.3 and the dated study guide. Rechecked the credit groups and progression gates before reconsidering the frozen schedules, interests, alignments and audience fields.
findings: The Dutch full-time bachelor has 60 EC in each year. The first year links programming and medical concepts, and the second applies epidemiology, healthcare information exchange and software development. The OER’s 18 EC elective group confirms the study-guide placeholder. The OER puts Medical Images and Signals and the 24 EC internship and thesis in semester two. The dated guide places Images and Signals in block 4.

The ordinary route requires 48 first-year EC to progress to year two and the full first year plus at least 48 EC from year two for third-year teaching and assessment. The academic and professional competency portfolio receives its summative assessment during Strategic Information Management. A pass is required before the internship and thesis. Open electives outside the preapproved list require approval, with the OER prescribing a request before 1 May of the preceding year.

Software construction, epidemiology and evidence synthesis strengthen the closest option. Biomedical sciences support a distinct signals and imaging option, and moving Image Processing to term six places it after linear algebra and systems. The third option combines health psychology, psychopathology, population health, data and evidence synthesis with communication and digital strategy. Pairwise schedule differences are 120, 52.5 and 127.5 EC each way. None of the UCR options provides UvA’s dedicated interoperability and clinical-practice sequence.

The scoped overlaps are in programming, software design, data handling, logic, public health, research, entrepreneurship, digital change, machine learning and image analysis. The required UvA internship and thesis and optional UCR research remain separate. Checked all 16 comparator titles and credits, 46 UCR course titles and descriptions, three concepts, five note anchors, alignment and source links.
